content: The document titled Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines: Driving Impact Through Programme Monitoring and Management includes a Web Annex (Annex B) that focuses on the alignment of indicators across global monitoring and evaluation frameworks. This publication, released by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2020, is available electronically under the ISBN 978-92-4-000437-5. The suggested citation for this annex is: Web Annex B. Indicator alignment across global monitoring and evaluation frameworks. In: Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines: Driving Impact Through Programme Monitoring and Management. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2020. The annex provides detailed information on the alignment of indicators used in global monitoring and evaluation frameworks. Indicators are categorized as consistent (C), similar (S), or related (R). A consistent indicator has identical numerator and denominator definitions across frameworks. A similar indicator shares basic definitions but differs in how the numerator or denominator is calculated. A related indicator is reflected only as a numerator, denominator, or disaggregation category in other frameworks. Blank cells indicate the absence of an equivalent indicator in a specific monitoring and evaluation framework. Examples of indicators include syphilis screening coverage during antenatal care (ANC) and AIDS-related mortality. The document also references the Global Fund for AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Modular Framework indicators (version 4, FY20).
